first_end.mechanism: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; 51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) orders that the listed Executive Orders, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:", in a two-column table headed 'No. Subject'; its entry "11314 Creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the military jet engine, military" names this order by number. A scan of the full held text of EO 12553 for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending finds those strings only inside table subjects (the words effectiveness and Suspending), not as operative wording, so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, 1986-02-25; that is an inference from the heading and signature block, not express wording.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The printed order creates a board of inquiry under section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, appoints its members, gives it the powers and duties of Title II of the Act, sets "on or before October 18th, 1966" for the Evendale dispute and, for any other strike, a report as soon as possible, and provides that the Board continues in existence after reporting. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes it by number ("11314 Creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the military jet engine, military"). The report date is a deadline, not an end, and no held source establishes the Board's actual report or discharge, so no earlier end or later event is recorded. The order states no end date of its own, and the by-number scan of held order texts finds no later order citing it.

Executive Order No. 11314
CREATING A BOARD OF INQUIRY TO REPORT ON CERTAIN LABOR
DISPUTES AFFECTING THE MILITARY JET ENGINE INDUSTRY, MILI­
TARY AIRCRAFT INDUSTRY, MILITARY ARMAMENT INDUSTRY AND
MILITARY ELECTRONICS INDUSTRY OF THE UNITED STATES
W H E R E A S, there have existed certain labor disputes between Gen­
eral Electric Company and certain of its employees represented by : 
International Union of Electrical Radio and Machine Workers, 
A F L -C IO ; International Association of Machinists and Aerospace 
Workers, A F L -C IO ; International Union, United Automobile, Aero­
space and A gricultural Implement Workers of America, A F L -C IO  ; 
International Union, Allied Industrial W orkers of America, A F L - 
CIO ; International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, A F L -C IO ; 
Sheet Metal W orkers’  International Association, A F L -C IO ; Ameri­
can Federation of Technical Engineers, A F L -C IO  ; American F lint 
Glass W orkers’  Union of North America, A F L -C IO ; United 
Electrical Radio and Machine W orkers of America; United Associa­
tion of Journeymen and Apprentices of the Plumbing and Pipe F itting 
Industry of the United States and Canada, A F L -C IO  ; United Steel­
workers of America, A F L -C IO ; International Union of Operating 
Engineers, A F L -C IO  ; International Brotherhood of Teamsters, 
Chauffeurs, Warehousemen and Helpers of America ; Pattern Makers’  
League of North America, A F L -C IO  ; International Brotherhood of 
Firemen and Oilers, A F L -C IO ; Syracuse Draftsmens Union; and
W H E R E A S, although a tentative resolution of these disputes was 
arrived at by the parties, or some of them, nevertheless there is a strike 
at the Evendale, Ohio, plant of General Electric Company by Local 
No. 647 of the International Union of the United Automobile, Aero­
space and Agricultural Implement Workers of America, A F L -C IO , 
and Locals 34 and 912 of the International Association of Machinists 
and Aerospace Workers, A F L -C IO , and there exists a threat that 
there will be further strikes at General Electric Company plants by 
one or more of the aforesaid international unions or local units 
thereof ; and
W H E R E A S, the existing strike at the Evendale, Ohio, plant of 
General Electric Company will, in my opinion, if permitted to con­
tinue, affect a substantial p art of the m ilitary jet engine industry, 
which industry is engaged in trade, commerce, transportation, trans­
mission, or communication among the several states or with foreign 
nations, or engaged in the production of goods for commerce, and which 
strike, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national safety ; and
W H E R E A S, threatened strikes at other General Electric Company 
plants will, in my opinion, if allowed to occur, affect a substantial 
p art of the military jet engine industry, m ilitary aircraft industry, 
m ilitary armament industry and m ilitary electronics industry, which 
industries are engaged in trade, commerce, transportation, transmis­
sion, or communication among the several states or with foreign na­
tions, or engaged in the production of goods for commerce, and which 
threatened strikes, if permitted to occur, will imperil the national 
safety ;
NOW T H E R E F O R E  by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act of 1947 (61 Stat. 
155; 29 U.S.C. 176), I  hereby create a Board of Inquiry, consisting 
of Mr. David L. Cole, Chairman, Mr. John Dunlop and Mr. Jacob 
Seidenberg, whom I  appoint to inquire into the issues involved in 
these disputes.
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 31, NO. 202— TUESDAY, OCTOBER 18, 1966

=== PDF page 12 of 52 ===
13420 THE PRESIDENT
The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title I I  of 
such Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance 
with the provisions of Section 206 of such Act. W ith respect to the 
dispute giving rise to the strike at Evendale, Ohio, plant it shall report 
on or before October 18th, 1966, and with respect to the dispute or 
disputes resulting in any other such strike, it shall report as soon as 
possible.
Upon the submission of its report or reports, the Board shall con­
tinue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required 
under such Act.

research_rationale:
EO 11314 (signed 1966-10-17; 31 FR 13419-13420 (Federal Register of October 18, 1966; PDF pages 11-12)) creates a board of inquiry under section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act of 1947 to inquire into labor disputes between General Electric Company and certain of its employees represented by a list of unions, recites a strike at the Evendale, Ohio, plant and threatened strikes at other General Electric plants affecting the military jet engine, military aircraft, military armament and military electronics industries, appoints David L. Cole (Chairman), John Dunlop and Jacob Seidenberg, gives the Board the powers and duties of Title II of that Act, directs it to report on the Evendale dispute "on or before October 18th, 1966" and on any other strike as soon as possible (the order's words are "it shall report as soon as" possible), and provides that upon submission of its report or reports the Board continues in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11314.txt); its printed number, title, page and signature date match the census register row. The dossier's clause inventory splits the order mid-sentence or omits its opening paragraphs, so I replaced it with one clause covering the printed order from its heading to its last operative sentence (characters 521-4809); the order has no numbered sections. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes the order by number in its revocation table, and that express revocation is the first end. The report date is a deadline, not an end; no report of this Board is held (a search of the held texts for the order's number and subject words found none), so no report or discharge date is recorded as a later event. Bounded search: the dossier's three machine searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts); the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order sets \"on or before October 18th, 1966\" for the Evendale dispute and, for any other strike, a report as soon as possible and says the Board continues in existence after reporting to perform functions required under the Act; it states no end date. A report date is a deadline, not an end. No held source establishes when the Board reported, whether the dispute settled, or whether the Board was ever discharged, so no earlier end is claimed. The by-number scan finds no held later order citing this order (its hits are copies of the order itself); EO 12553 names it in the number column of its revocation table, which the regex scan does not match, and I found that entry by reading. The Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches record no hit.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order creates the Board, appoints its named members, gives it the Act's powers, sets its report date and continues it after reporting. The appointments are one-time acts; the members' service depends on the Board, which exists only under the order. No held source shows when the Board reported or was discharged, so no earlier end is asserted. The order creates no fund, delegation or authority outside the Board.","savings_check":"Savings: none in EO 12553 or in this order; nothing continues independently of the order.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 lists the order by number with no 'in part' limit, so the single corrected clause ends on the revocation date. No held source records an amendment of this order."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception or pending-matter wording: a scan of its full held text for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending finds those strings only inside table subjects. The revocation therefore leaves no part of this order in operation. The order created no continuing right or fund; whatever the Board did before the revocation is a completed fact whose dates are not established by a held source.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The printed order creates a board of inquiry under section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, appoints its members, gives it the powers and duties of Title II of the Act, sets a report due by March 8, 1967 (the order's words are "with the provisions of Section 206 of such Act on or before March 8," followed by 1967 on the next line), and provides that the Board continues in existence after reporting. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes it by number ("11329 Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the shipbuilding and repair"). The report date is a deadline, not an end, and no held source establishes the Board's actual report or discharge, so no earlier end or later event is recorded. The order states no end date of its own, and the by-number scan of held order texts finds no later order citing it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11329
CREATING A BOARD OF INQUIRY TO REPORT ON A LABOR DISPUTE
AFFECTING THE SHIPBUILDING AND REPAIR INDUSTRIES OF THE
UNITED STATES
W H E R E A S , there exists a labor dispute between the Pacific Coast 
Shipbuilders’ Association, Alameda, California, representing Lock­
heed Shipbuilding and Construction Company, Seattle, Washington,  
Bethlehem Steel Company, San Francisco, California, Lake Union  
Dry Docks Company, Seattle, Washington, Pacific Coast Engineering  
Company, Alameda, California, Albina Engine and Machine Works,  
Portland, Oregon, Northwest Marine Iron Works, Portland, Oregon,  
Todd Shipyards Corporation, Seattle, Washington and Alameda,  
California, Guy F. Atkinson Company, Portland, Oregon, Willamette  
Iron and Steel Company, Portland, Oregon, and certain of their em­
ployees represented by the International Brotherhood of Electrical  
Workers, A F L -C I O ; and
W H E R E A S , such dispute has resulted in a strike which will, in my 
opinion, if permitted to continue, affect a substantial part of the ship­
building and repair industries, which industries are engaged in trade,  
commerce, transportation, transmission, or communication among the  
several States or with foreign nations, or engaged m the production of  
goods for commerce, and which strike, if permitted to continue, will  
imperil the national safety:
N O W  T H E R E F O R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act of 1947 (61 Stat.  
155: 29 U.S.C. 176),H  hereby create a Board of Inquiry, consisting of  
Mr. J. Keith Mann, Chairman, Mr. George E. Reedy and Mr. Paul D.  
Hanlon, whom I  appoint to inquire into the issues involved m this
dispute.
The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title I I  of  
such Act. The Board shall report to the President m accordance  
with the provisions of Section 206 of such Act on or before March 8,  
1967.
Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence  
to perform such other functions as may be required under such Act.

research_rationale:
EO 11329 (signed 1967-03-02; 32 FR 3811 (Federal Register of March 8, 1967; PDF page 7)) creates a board of inquiry under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act of 1947 to inquire into a labor dispute between the Pacific Coast Shipbuilders' Association, representing named shipbuilding and repair companies, and certain of their employees represented by the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, which had resulted in a strike, appoints J. Keith Mann (Chairman), George E. Reedy and Paul D. Hanlon, gives the Board the powers and duties of Title II of that Act, directs it to report to the President in accordance "with the provisions of Section 206 of such Act on or before March 8," 1967, and provides that upon submission of its report the Board continues in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11329.txt); its printed number, title, page and signature date match the census register row. The dossier's clause inventory splits the order mid-sentence or omits its opening paragraphs, so I replaced it with one clause covering the printed order from its heading to its last operative sentence (characters 516-2600); the order has no numbered sections. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes the order by number in its revocation table, and that express revocation is the first end. The report date is a deadline, not an end; no report of this Board is held (a search of the held texts for the order's number and subject words found none), so no report or discharge date is recorded as a later event. Bounded search: the dossier's three machine searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts); the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order sets a report due by March 8, 1967 (the order's words are \"with the provisions of Section 206 of such Act on or before March 8,\" followed by 1967 on the next line) and says the Board continues in existence after reporting to perform functions required under the Act; it states no end date. A report date is a deadline, not an end. No held source establishes when the Board reported, whether the dispute settled, or whether the Board was ever discharged, so no earlier end is claimed. The by-number scan finds no held later order citing this order (its hits are copies of the order itself); EO 12553 names it in the number column of its revocation table, which the regex scan does not match, and I found that entry by reading. The Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches record no hit.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order creates the Board, appoints its named members, gives it the Act's powers, sets its report date and continues it after reporting. The appointments are one-time acts; the members' service depends on the Board, which exists only under the order. No held source shows when the Board reported or was discharged, so no earlier end is asserted. The order creates no fund, delegation or authority outside the Board.","savings_check":"Savings: none in EO 12553 or in this order; nothing continues independently of the order.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 lists the order by number with no 'in part' limit, so the single corrected clause ends on the revocation date. No held source records an amendment of this order."}

The order created no continuing right or fund; whatever the Board did before the revocation is a completed fact whose dates are not established by a held source.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Clause 1 rewrites the first sentence of subsection 305(a) of EO 10647 so that at least once every twelve months the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission surveys appointments made under section 710(b)(1) of the Act. It continued, amended, until the order ended: first end EO 12919, 1994-06-03, which supersedes or revokes EO 11355 by number in section 904(a)(6) and EO 10647 in section 904(a)(4). Later event, not an end: EO 12107, effective 1979-01-01, substitutes Office of Personnel Management words for Civil Service Commission words in the orders listed in its section 2-101(b), which include EO 11355. Before: the survey duty lies with the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission. After: the substitution rule replaces Civil Service Commission with Office of Personnel Management and the Chairman with the Director of that Office, so the duty lies with the Director of the Office of Personnel Management; the held sources print no consolidated text of the sentence after substitution.

later_events.mechanism: amendment by word substitution, recorded as an event and not an end: section 2-101 of EO 12107 (signed 1978-12-28; 44 FR 1055, Federal Register of January 3, 1979) amends each listed order by substituting the words Office of Personnel Management for Civil Service Commission and the words Director, Office of Personnel Management for Chairman, Civil Service Commission, and EO 11355 is listed in subsection 2-101(b); section 2-404 says "Order, this Order shall be effective on January 1, 1979." Before: clause 1 makes the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission responsible for the annual survey. After: the Director of the Office of Personnel Management carries that duty; the exact post-substitution wording is not printed in the held sources. The substitution does not touch clauses 2 and 3, which name no Commission or Chairman.

research_rationale:
EO 11355 (signed 1967-05-26; 32 FR 7803, Federal Register of May 30, 1967) amends EO 10647 of November 28, 1955 on appointments under the Defense Production Act of 1950: clause 1 rewrites the first sentence of subsection 305(a) (at least once every twelve months the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission surveys appointments made under section 710(b)(1) of the Act), clause 2 rewrites paragraph (1) of subsection 305(b) (the statistical report of appointments) and clause 3 revokes Part II of EO 10647. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11355.txt, PDF page 7) and confirmed its number, title, page and date against the census register; the three numbered clauses are the complete inventory, and the opening authority paragraph is a lead-in, not a command. EO 12919 (signed 1994-06-03) supersedes or revokes EO 11355 by number in section 904(a)(6), and EO 10647 in section 904(a)(4); that express revocation is the first end of every clause. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments each amending clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends. EO 12107 (signed 1978-12-28, effective 1979-01-01) lists EO 11355 in its section 2-101(b) and substitutes Office of Personnel Management words for Civil Service Commission words; it is recorded as a later event of clause 1, not an end. savings_residuals.reason: EO 12919 section 903 keeps previously issued orders and actions in effect only "except as they are inconsistent with this order" or are revoked, and section 904(a) revokes this order by name, so its commands do not continue. Section 903 also provides that nothing "in this order shall affect the validity or force of anything done under previous" delegations or other assignment of authority under the Act; surveys, reports and appointments made under EO 10647 as amended by this order are therefore accrued completed acts.

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including the Defense Production 
Act of 1950, as amended (64 Stat. 798; 50 U .S.C  App. 2061, e t seq .)  
and section 301 of title 3, United States Code, and as Commander in Chief 
of the Armed Forces of the United States, it is hereby ordered as follows
PART 1 — PURPOSE, POLICY AND IMPLEMENTATION
Section 101. P u rp o se. This order delegates authorities and addresses national 
defense industrial resource policies and programs under the Defense Produc­
tion Act of 1950, as amended (“the A ct”), except for the amendments to 
Title III of the Act in the Energy Security Act of 1980 and telecommunication 
authorities under Executive Order No. 12472.
Sec. 102. P o licy . The United States must have an industrial and technology 
base capable of meeting national defense requirements, and capable of con­
tributing to the technological superiority o f its defense equipment in peace­
time and in times of national emergency. The domestic industrial and techno- 
logical base is the foundation for national defense preparedness. The authori­
ties provided in the Act shall be used to strengthen this base and to ensure 
it is capable of responding to all threats to the national security of the 
United States.
Sec. 103. G en era l F u n ctio n s.  Federal departments and agencies responsible 
for defense acquisition (or for industrial resources needed to support defense 
acquisition) shall:
(a) Identify requirements for the full spectrum of national security emer­
gencies, including m ilitary, industrial, and essential civilian demand;
(b) Assess continually the capability of the domestic industrial and techno­
logical base to satisfy requirements in peacetime and times of national 
emergency, specifically evaluating the availability o f adequate industrial 
resource and production sources, including subcontractors and suppliers 
materials, skilled labor, and professional and technical personnel;
(c) Be prepared, in the event of a potential threat to the security of 
the United States, to take actions necessary to ensure the availability of 
adequate industrial resources and production capability, including services 
and critical technology for national defense requirements;
(d) Improve the efficiency and responsiveness to defense requirements 
of the domestic industrial base; and
(e) Foster cooperation between the defense and commercial sectors for 
research and development and for acquisition of materials, components 
and equipment to enhance industrial base efficiency and responsiveness
Sec. 104. Im p le m e n ta tio n , (a) The National Security Council is the principal 
forum for consideration and resolution of national security resource prepared­
ness policy. -
(b) The Director, Federal Emergency' Management Agency (“Director 
FEM A”) shall:
(1) Serve as an advisor to the National Security Council on issues 
of national security resource preparedness and on the use of the 
authorities and functions delegated by this order-

(1) The Secretary of Agriculture with respect to food resources,  
food resource facilities, and the domestic distribution of farm equip­
ment and commercial fertilizer;.
(2) The Secretary of Energy with respect to all forms of energy;
(3) The Secretary of Health and Human Services with respect to  
health resources;
(4) The Secretary of Transportation with respect to all forms of  
civil transportation;
(5) ;  The Secretary of Defense with respect to water resources; and
(6) The Secretary of Commerce for all other materials, services,

C & l f  The Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the heads of those

administer the Defense Priorities and Allocations System (“DPAS”) regula­
tions that will be used to implement the authority of the President conferred

to the-Secretary of Defense, and the heads of other departments and agencies

fcl The Director, FEMA, shall attempt to resolve issues or disagreements

required under subsection 101(b) of the Act. This finding shall be submitted  
for the President’s approval through the Assistant to the President for Na­
tional Security Affairs. Upon such approval the head, of the Federal depart-

Sec. 202. Determinations.  The authority delegated by section 201 of this 
order may be used only to support programs that have been determined 
in writing as necessary or appropriate to promote the national defense:
(a) By the Secretary of Defense with respect to military production and 
construction, military assistance to foreign nations, stockpiling, outer space, 
and directly related activities;
(b) By the Secretary of Energy with respect to energy production and 
construction, distribution and use, and directly related activities; and
(c) By the Director, FEMA, with respect to essential civilian needs support­
ing national defense, including civil defense and continuity of government 
and directly related activities.
Sec. 203. Maximizing Domestic  Energy Supplies.  The authority of the Presi­
dent to perform the functions provided by subsection 101(c) of the Act 
is delegated to the Secretary of Commerce, who shall redelegate to the 
Secretary of Energy the authority to make the findings described in subsection 
101(c)(2)(A) that the m aterials (including equipment), services, and facilities 
are critical and essential. The Secretary of Commerce shall make the finding 
described in subsection 101(c)(2)(A) of the Act that the materials (including 
equipment), services, or facilities are scarce, and the finding described in 
subsection 101(c)(2)(B) that it is necessary to use the authority provided 
by subsection 101(c)(1).
Sec. 204. Chemical and Biological Warfare.  The authority of the President 
conferred by subsection 104(b) of the Act is delegated to the Secretary 
of Defense. This authority may not be further delegated by the Secretary.
PART III— EXPANSION OF PRODUCTIVE CAPACITY AND SUPPLY
Sec. 301. (a) Financing Institution Guarantees.  To expedite or expand produc­
tion and deliveries or services under government contracts for the procure­
ment of industrial resources or critical technology items essential to the 
national defense, the head of each Federal department or agency engaged 
in procurement for the national defense (referred to as “agency head” in 
this part) and the President and Chairman o f the Export-Import Bank of 
the United States (in cases involving capacity expansion, technological d evel­
opment, or production in foreign countries) are authorized to guarantee 
in w hole or in part any public or private financing institution, subject 
to provisions of section 301 of the Act. Guarantees shall be made in consulta­
tion with the Department of the Treasury as to the terms and conditions 
thereof. The Director of the Office of Management and Budget (“OMB”) 
shall be informed when such guarantees are to be made.
(b) Direct Loan Guarantees.  To expedite or expand production and deliv­
eries or services under government contracts for the procurement of industrial 
resources or critical technology items essential to the national defense, each 
agency head is authorized to make direct loan guarantees from funds appro­
priated to their agency for Title HI.
(c) Fiscal Agent.  Each Federal Reserve Bank is designated and authorized 
to act, on behalf of any guaranteeing agency, as fiscal agent in the making 
of guarantee contracts and in otherwise carrying out the purposes of section 
301 of the Act.
(d) Regulations.  The Board of Governors o f the Federal Reserve System 
is authorized, after consultation with heads of guaranteeing departments 
and agencies, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the Director, OMB, to

Sec. 303. Purchase Commitments,  (a) In order to carry out the objectives  
of the Act, and subject to the provisions of section 303 thereof, an agency  
head is authorized to make provision for purchases of, or commitments  
to purchase, an industrial resource or a critical technology item for govern­
ment use or resale.
(b) Materials acquired under section 303 of the Act that exceed the needs  
of the programs under the Act may be transferred to the National Defense  
Stockpile, if such transfer is determined by the Secretary of Defense as  
the National Defense Stockpile Manager to be in the public interest.
Sec. 304. Subsidy Payments.  In order to ensure the supply of raw or non-  
processed materials from high-cost sources, an agency head is authorized  
to make subsidy payments, after consultation with the Secretary of the  
Treasury and the Director, OMB, and subject to the provisions of section  
303(c) of the Act.
Sec. 305. Determinations and Findings.  When carrying out the authorities  
in sections 301 through 303 of this order, an agency head is authorized  
to make the required determinations, judgments, statements, certifications,  
and findings, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, Secretary of  
Energy or Director, FEMA, as appropriate. The agency head shall provide  
a copy of the determination, judgment, statement, certification, or finding  
to the Director, OMB, to the Director, FEMA, and, when appropriate, to  
the Secretary of the Treasury.
Sec. 306. Strategic and Critical Materials, [a)  The Secretary of the Interior  
in consultation with the Secretary of Defense as the National Defense Stock­
pile Manager and subject to the provisions of section 303 of the Act, is  
authorized to encourage the exploration, development, and mining of critical  
and strategic.materials and other materials.
(b) An agency head is authorized, pursuant to section 303(g) of the Act,  
to make provision for the development of substitutes for strategic and critical  
materials, critical components, critical technology items, and other industrial  
resources to aid the national defense.
(c) An agency head is authorized, pursuant to section 303(a)(1)(B) of  
the Act, to make provisions to encourage the exploration, development  
and mining of critical and strategic materials and other materials.
Sec. 307 . Government-owned Equipment.  An agency head is authorized,  
pursuant to section 303(e) of the Act, to install additional equipment, facili­
ties, processes, or improvements to facilities owned by the government and  
to install government-owned equipment in industrial facilities owned by  
private persons.

in-Chief of the Unified and Specified Commands and other items within

(b) Each agency head shall take appropriate action to ensure that critical

Sec. 311. Strengthening Domestic Capability.  An agency head, in accordance

ize, and expand the productive capacities of domestic sources for critical  
components, critical technology items, and industrial resources essential  
for the execution of the national security strategy of the United States.
Sec. 312. Modernization o f Equipment.  An agency head, in accordance with  
section 108(b) of the Act, may utilize the authority of Title III of the Act  
to guarantee the purchase or lease of advance manufacturing equipment  
and any related services with respect to any such equipment for purposes  
of the Act.

President by section 309 of the Act with respect to offsets are delegated

PART VI— EMPLOYMENT OF PERSONNEL
Sec. 601. National Defense Executive Reserve, (a) In accordance with section 
710(e) of the Act, there is established in the Executive Branch a National 
Defense Executive Reserve (“NDER”) composed of persons of recognized 
expertise from various segments of the private sector and from government 
(except full-time federal employees) for training for employment in executive 
positions in the Federal Government in the event of an emergency that 
requires such employment.
(b) The head of any department or agency may establish a unit of the 
NDER in the department or agency and train members of that unit.
(c) The head of each department or agency with an NDER unit is authorized 
to exercise the President’s authority to employ civilian personnel in accord­
ance with section 703(a) of the Act when activating all or a part of its 
NDER unit. The exercise of this authority shall be subject to the provisions 
of subsections 601(d) and (e) of this order and shall not be redelegated.
(d) The head of a department or agency may activate an NDER unit, 
in whole or in part, upon the written determination that an emergency 
affecting the national security or defense preparedness of the United States 
exists and that the activation of the unit is necessary to carry out the 
emergency program functions of the department or agency.
(e) At least 72 hours prior to activating the NDER unit, the head of 
the department or agency shall notify, in writing, the Assistant to the Presi­
dent for National Security Affairs of the impending activation and provide 
a copy of the determination required under subsection 601(d) of this order
(f) The Director, FEMA, shall coordinate the NDER program activities

for appropriate guidance for recruitment, training, and activation, and issue 
necessary rules and guidance in connection with the program.

quirement or condition with respect to the activation of any NDER unit,

applies only as long as sections 703(a) an(K710(e) of the Act are in effect.

The authority delegated by this section shall not be redelegated.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The printed order creates a board of inquiry under section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, appoints its members, gives it the powers and duties of Title II of the Act, sets a report due by October 2, 1968 (the order's words are "on or before October 2," followed by 1968 on the next line), and provides that the Board continues in existence after reporting. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes it by number ("11431 Creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the maritime industry"). The report date is a deadline, not an end, and no held source establishes the Board's actual report or discharge, so no earlier end or later event is recorded. The order states no end date of its own, and the by-number scan of held order texts finds no later order citing it.

Executive Order 11431
CREATING A BOARD OF INQUIRY TO REPORT ON CERTAIN LABOR
DISPUTES AFFECTING THE MARITIME INDUSTRY OF THE UNITED
STATES
W H E RE A S, there exist certain labor disputes between employers 
(or associations by which such employers are represented in collective 
bargaining conferences) who are (1) steamship companies or who are 
engaged as operators or agents for ships engaged in service from or 
to Atlantic and Gulf Coast ports from Searsport, Maine, to Browns- 
ville, Texas, or from or to other ports of the United States or its ter­
ritories or possessions, (2) contracting stevedores, (3) contracting 
marine carpenters, (4) lighterage operators, or (5) other employers 
engaged in related or associated pier activities and certain of their 
employees represented by the International Longshoremen’s Associa­
tion, A F L -C IO ; and
W H E RE A S, such disputes have resulted in a threatened strike 
which if permitted to occur, will, in my opinion, affect a substantial 
part of the maritime industry, an industry engaged in trade, commerce, 
transportation, transmission, or communication among the several 
States and with foreign nations, and which strike will, if permitted 
to occur, imperil the national health and safety.
„ NOW, TH E R E FO R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 206 o f the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 (61 Stat. 
155; 29 U.S.C. 176), I  hereby create a Board o f Inquiry, consisting o f:
Honorable David L. Cole, as Chairman, Honorable Peter Seitz, and
The Right Reverend Monsignor George G. Higgins,
as Members, whom I hereby appoint to inquire into the issues involved 
in such disputes.
The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II  
o f such Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance 
with the provisions of Section 206 o f such Act on or before October 2, 
1968.
Upon the submission of its report, the Board shall continue in ex­
istence to perform such other functions as may be required under such 
Act.

research_rationale:
EO 11431 (signed 1968-09-30; 33 FR 14697 (Federal Register of October 2, 1968; PDF page 7)) creates a board of inquiry under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 to inquire into labor disputes between steamship companies, contracting stevedores, contracting marine carpenters, lighterage operators and other employers in related pier activities at Atlantic and Gulf Coast and other ports and certain of their employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, which had resulted in a threatened strike, appoints David L. Cole (Chairman), Peter Seitz and Monsignor George G. Higgins, gives the Board the powers and duties of Title II of that Act, directs it to report to the President in accordance with section 206 "on or before October 2," 1968, and provides that upon submission of its report the Board continues in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11431.txt); its printed number, title, page and signature date match the census register row. The dossier's clause inventory splits the order mid-sentence or omits its opening paragraphs, so I replaced it with one clause covering the printed order from its heading to its last operative sentence (characters 518-2542); the order has no numbered sections. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes the order by number in its revocation table, and that express revocation is the first end. The report date is a deadline, not an end; no report of this Board is held (a search of the held texts for the order's number and subject words found none), so no report or discharge date is recorded as a later event. Bounded search: the dossier's three machine searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts); the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order sets a report due by October 2, 1968 (the order's words are \"on or before October 2,\" followed by 1968 on the next line) and says the Board continues in existence after reporting to perform functions required under the Act; it states no end date. A report date is a deadline, not an end. No held source establishes when the Board reported, whether the dispute settled, or whether the Board was ever discharged, so no earlier end is claimed. The by-number scan finds no held later order citing this order (its hits are copies of the order itself); EO 12553 names it in the number column of its revocation table, which the regex scan does not match, and I found that entry by reading. The Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches record no hit.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order creates the Board, appoints its named members, gives it the Act's powers, sets its report date and continues it after reporting. The appointments are one-time acts; the members' service depends on the Board, which exists only under the order. No held source shows when the Board reported or was discharged, so no earlier end is asserted. The order creates no fund, delegation or authority outside the Board.","savings_check":"Savings: none in EO 12553 or in this order; nothing continues independently of the order.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 lists the order by number with no 'in part' limit, so the single corrected clause ends on the revocation date. No held source records an amendment of this order."}

The revocation therefore leaves no part of this order in operation. The order created no continuing right or fund; whatever the Board did before the revocation is a completed fact whose dates are not established by a held source.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's sole operative sentence suspends section 6372 of title 10 of the United States Code under the authority of section 6386(c) of that title. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11436 Suspending provisions of section 6372 of title 10, U.S.C., relating to retirement or retention on the"). The order states no duration, so no own-terms end applies. Earlier candidate ends that do not name this order, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; neither is the end because neither names EO 11436): (1) the National Emergencies Act, Pub. L. 94-412 (Sept. 14, 1976), whose section 101(a) terminated, two years after enactment, powers possessed as a result of national emergencies then in effect; its section 502(a)(8) provides that the Act shall not apply to "Sections 3313, 6386(c), and 8313 of title 10, United States" Code, so that termination did not reach the section 6386(c) authority this order rests on (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10976_Pub._L._94-412_National_Emergencies_Act_sec._101_a_90_Stat._1255_Sept._14_1976_status_d1e4940870.txt, text sha256 9af91c5062c556d26e97baaa68d89a4aa6cbfbb51937898bc13ef801d78a350). (2) The Defense Officer Personnel Management Act, Pub. L. 96-513 (Dec. 12, 1980), whose section 335 provides that "The following sections of chapter 573 are repealed:" and lists, among others, sections 6372 (the section this order suspends) and 6386 (the section whose subsection (c) is the order's authority), effective September 15, 1981 under section 701(a) (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11436_Defense_Officer_Personnel_Management_Act_Pub._L._96-513_Dec._12_1980_94_Stat._2835_in_bdcccb89ac.txt, text sha256 c3ab6a35c6abc89d1a7cf8da82a3857809878054424edc8731240edb46dc7970). Section 702 of that Act preserves the suspended status of a provision that is amended, not repealed, so it does not apply to the repealed section 6372; section 703 preserves matured rights, penalties and proceedings. After September 15, 1981 the suspension had no statutory provision left to operate on, but under the ruling the repeal is a disclosed candidate, and the order's end remains the instrument that names it.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 12121 (signed 1979-02-26, 44 FR 11195) amends section 1-102 of EO 12083 by adding two members to the Energy Coordinating Committee, "The Director of the Community Services Administration." and "The Chairman of the Council on Wage and Price Stability."; its only command is that addition and it has no own-terms end. EO 12083 (held FR text of September 27, 1978) has no sunset. First end: EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17, 47 FR 36099), whose section 20 reads "Sec. 20. Executive O rder No. 12083, as amended, establishing the Energy" (continuing on the next line: Coordinating Committee, is revoked). EO 12379 does not name EO 12121; it revokes EO 12083 as amended, and because EO 12121's whole operative content is a textual addition to section 1-102 of EO 12083, the revocation of EO 12083 as amended removes the section it amends and ends the clause. EO 12379 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1982-08-17. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note on this order reads "Revoked by: EO 12379, August 17, 1982". Later event: EO 12156 (signed 1979-09-10, 44 FR 53073) adds member (z), the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, to section 1-102 as amended by EO 12121 and leaves the two members added by EO 12121 in place, so it is a later amendment event, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21, strike-and-insert). Disclosed earlier candidates under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; neither names EO 12121, so neither is the end): (1) the Community Services Administration. An Office of the Federal Register editorial note in the held 1989 codification text (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_12344.txt, sha256 747052eb81a27f8e0040ae9c8bd5f478841e46df4e9ba7c683587599624bdbf8; the same note is in EO_12160.txt) states that "The Community Services Administration was abolished through" the repeal of the Economic Opportunity Act of 1964 "by Pub . L. 97-35 (95 Stat . 519, 42 U.S.C. 2941)", the Omnibus Reconciliation Act of 1981. The note gives no effective date and the statute is not held, so the date the Director's office ceased is not fixed by a held source beyond falling in or after 1981 and before EO 12379. (2) The Council on Wage and Price Stability. An editorial note in the held 1989 codification text (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_12154.txt, sha256 bff5d25514c124e6fc4decb93eeae7ae824204d396dcb03bca755207208da54a) states that "The Council on Wage and Price Stability was abolished by Execu-" tive Order 12288 of Jan. 29, 1981. The held Federal Register text of EO 12288 (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12288.txt, sha256 995315c4dc9f143a80b008ebfff389f119a3d67afbba6f82fc37508a35da5e6d) does not abolish the Council: it revokes EO 12092 and authorizes the heads of agencies, "including" the Council on Wage and Price Stability, to take steps to terminate actions adopted under EO 12092, which treats the Council as still existing. No held source fixes when the Council ceased, so it is not established that both offices had ceased before 1982-08-17. Even if both had ceased, the Energy Coordinating Committee continued under EO 12083 with its other members, the added entries remained text of section 1-102, and under the ruling the end is the instrument that revokes the amended order, EO 12379. Disclosed alternative reading: if a reviewer holds that an order not named by number is not ended by the revocation of its amended parent, no first end is shown in the held sources.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The lead clause recites the authority, including the Federal Advisory Committee Act, states the purpose to increase the membership and extend the life of the President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government, and directs that Executive Order 12369 be amended as follows; it is the instruction that carries subsections (a) and (b). Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 orders that the listed Executive Orders, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and lists the number 12398 in the No. column of its revocation table (offset 26972 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt). This is an express revocation that names this order. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the first-end date is its signing date, 1986-02-25; that is a reading of the text, not express wording, and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and filing date 1986-02-26 are not effective dates. EO 12534 (signed 1985-09-30; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12534.txt, sha256 2f7a5c13126573ec9fb7f10631df9e25cac3065f405355c469a0222363ab443c) revokes, in section 3(b), Executive Order No. 12369 establishing the President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government, among orders that established committees that have terminated or been abolished by statute or whose work is completed; its section 5 reads "Sec. 5 This Order shall be effective September 30,1985." It names the parent order (without the words as amended) but not this amending order, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments it is a disclosed earlier candidate end (1985-09-30), not the end.

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and law s of the  
United States of Am erica, and to eliminate Executive Orders that are no  
longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Subsection (b) restates section 4(b) of EO 12369 so that, in accordance with the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended, "the Committee shall terminate on June 30, 1983, unless" sooner extended. Later amendments of the same sentence are recorded as later events that change the date and do not end the clause: EO 12429 (signed 1983-06-28) restates it with October 30, 1983, EO 12447 (signed 1983-10-27) with December 31, 1983 and EO 12455 (signed 1983-12-29) with January 31, 1984, each as a rewrite of the whole sentence that changes its substance (the date) while the clause continues, amended, until the order ends. The last held sunset is 1984-01-31 ("unless sooner extended", EO 12455); no held source shows whether the Committee was extended again or the date on which it in fact ceased, although EO 12534 lists its establishing order among committees that have terminated or been abolished by statute or whose work is completed. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 orders that the listed Executive Orders, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and lists the number 12398 in the No. column of its revocation table (offset 26972 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt). This is an express revocation that names this order. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the first-end date is its signing date, 1986-02-25; that is a reading of the text, not express wording, and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and filing date 1986-02-26 are not effective dates.

later_events.mechanism: restatement of section 4(b) of EO 12369 by EO 12429 (signed 1983-06-28; 48 FR 30087, Federal Register of June 30, 1983; no effective-date wording, read as effective on signing), recorded as a later event and not an end under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments: section 4(b) of EO 12369, as amended, is further amended to read that the Committee shall terminate on October 30, 1983, unless sooner extended. Before: the sentence installed by EO 12398 reads that, in accordance with the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended, the Committee shall terminate on June 30, 1983, unless sooner extended. After: the sentence reads that the Committee shall terminate on October 30, 1983, unless sooner extended. The rewrite replaces the whole sentence and changes its substance (the termination date); it also drops the words in accordance with the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended.

Executive Order 12398 of December 31, 1982
President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the  
United States of America, including the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as  
amended (5 U.S.C. App. I), and in order to increase the membership and  
extend the life of the President’s Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the  
Federal Government, it is hereby ordered that Executive Order No. 12369 of  
June 30,1982, is amended as follows:
(a) The second sentence of Section 1(a) shall read: “The Committee shall be  
composed of not more than 170 members appointed by the President from  
among citizens in private life.’’.
(b) Section 4(b) shall read: “In accordance with the Federal Advisory Commit­
tee Act, as amended, the Committee shall terminate on June 30, 1983, unless  
sooner extended.”.
THE WHITE HOUSE,  
D ecem b er 31, 1982.

research_rationale:
EO 12398 (signed 1982-12-31; 48 FR 377, Federal Register of January 5, 1983) was read in full in the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12398.txt. It amends Executive Order 12369 (President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government): the lead recital and instruction (to increase the membership and extend the life of the Survey), subsection (a) (the Committee is composed of not more than 170 members appointed by the President from among citizens in private life) and subsection (b) (section 4(b) restated so that, in accordance with the Federal Advisory Committee Act, the Committee terminates on June 30, 1983, unless sooner extended). The dossier evidence for the EO 12553 revocation was re-read against the held EO 12553 text, whose revocation table lists 12398. Later orders read in their held Federal Register texts and recorded as later events of subsection (b): EO 12429 (signed 1983-06-28) restates section 4(b) with the date October 30, 1983; EO 12447 (signed 1983-10-27) with December 31, 1983; EO 12455 (signed 1983-12-29) with January 31, 1984, each unless sooner extended. EO 12534 (signed 1985-09-30; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12534.txt, sha256 2f7a5c13126573ec9fb7f10631df9e25cac3065f405355c469a0222363ab443c) revokes, in section 3(b), Executive Order No. 12369 establishing the President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government, among orders that established committees that have terminated or been abolished by statute or whose work is completed; its section 5 reads "Sec. 5 This Order shall be effective September 30,1985." It names the parent order (without the words as amended) but not this amending order, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments it is a disclosed earlier candidate end (1985-09-30), not the end. Bounded search: the dossier's three machine searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts); the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; full reads of EO 12553, EO 12429, EO 12447, EO 12455 and EO 12534 in their held FR texts. Under the owner rulings of 2026-10-21 (unnamed instruments and strike-and-insert) and 2026-10-28 the end is EO 12553, the three amendments of section 4(b) are later events, and the parent revocation and the last held scheduled sunset are disclosed candidates.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole paragraph, in order to extend the life of the President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government, restates section 4(b) of Executive Order 12369, as amended, so that the Committee terminates on October 30, 1983, unless sooner extended. The same sentence was rewritten by EO 12447 (signed 1983-10-27, December 31, 1983) and EO 12455 (signed 1983-12-29, January 31, 1984); both are recorded as later events that change the date and are not ends of this clause. The last held sunset is 1984-01-31 ("unless sooner extended", EO 12455); no held source shows whether the Committee was extended again or the date on which it in fact ceased, although EO 12534 lists its establishing order among committees that have terminated or been abolished by statute or whose work is completed. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 orders that the listed Executive Orders, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and lists the number 12429 in the No. column of its revocation table (offset 27022 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt). This is an express revocation that names this order. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the first-end date is its signing date, 1986-02-25; that is a reading of the text, not express wording, and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and filing date 1986-02-26 are not effective dates. EO 12534 (signed 1985-09-30; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12534.txt, sha256 2f7a5c13126573ec9fb7f10631df9e25cac3065f405355c469a0222363ab443c) revokes, in section 3(b), Executive Order No. 12369 establishing the President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government, among orders that established committees that have terminated or been abolished by statute or whose work is completed; its section 5 reads "Sec. 5 This Order shall be effective September 30,1985." It names the parent order (without the words as amended) but not this amending order, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments it is a disclosed earlier candidate end (1985-09-30), not the end.

later_events.mechanism: restatement of section 4(b) of EO 12369 by EO 12447 (signed 1983-10-27; 48 FR 50055, Federal Register of October 31, 1983; no effective-date wording, read as effective on signing), recorded as a later event and not an end under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments: section 4(b) of EO 12369, as amended, is further amended to read that the Committee shall terminate on December 31, 1983, unless sooner extended. Before: the sentence installed by this order reads that the Committee shall terminate on October 30, 1983, unless sooner extended. After: the sentence reads that the Committee shall terminate on December 31, 1983, unless sooner extended. The rewrite replaces the whole sentence and changes its substance (the termination date).

EO 12429 (signed 1983-06-28; 48 FR 30087, Federal Register of June 30, 1983) was read in full in the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12429.txt. In order to extend the life of the President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government, it further amends section 4(b) of Executive Order 12369, as amended, to read that the Committee shall terminate on October 30, 1983, unless sooner extended. The dossier evidence for the EO 12553 revocation was re-read against the held EO 12553 text, whose revocation table lists 12429. Later orders read in their held Federal Register texts and recorded as later events: EO 12447 (signed 1983-10-27) restates the same sentence with December 31, 1983, and EO 12455 (signed 1983-12-29) with January 31, 1984, each unless sooner extended. EO 12534 (signed 1985-09-30; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12534.txt, sha256 2f7a5c13126573ec9fb7f10631df9e25cac3065f405355c469a0222363ab443c) revokes, in section 3(b), Executive Order No. 12369 establishing the President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government, among orders that established committees that have terminated or been abolished by statute or whose work is completed; its section 5 reads "Sec. 5 This Order shall be effective September 30,1985." It names the parent order (without the words as amended) but not this amending order, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments it is a disclosed earlier candidate end (1985-09-30), not the end. Bounded search: the dossier's three machine searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts); the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; full reads of EO 12553, EO 12447, EO 12455 and EO 12534 in their held FR texts. Under the owner rulings of 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-28 the end is EO 12553, the later sunset amendments are later events, and the parent revocation and the last held sunset are disclosed.

EO 12891 (signed 1994-01-15; 59 FR 2935-2937, Federal Register of January 20, 1994) was read in the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12891.txt (PDF pages 21-23 of the capture; the following pages belong to neighbouring documents). Identity, page and date confirmed from the printed heading, page numbers and signature date. The order establishes the Advisory Committee on Human Radiation Experiments (section 1), defines human radiation experiments in two categories and directs advice on specific experiments and the review period (section 2(a)), sets the Committee's evaluation functions (section 2(b)), provides information, compensation and funding (section 3), and assigns the President's Federal Advisory Committee Act functions to the Human Radiation Interagency Working Group, terminates the Committee 30 days after its final report and disclaims enforceable rights (section 4). The 18 clauses in the inventory were compared with the printed order from its heading through its signature: they cover every subsection and item; the enacting clause is not a command. The dossier evidence for EO 13062 was re-read against its held text: section 3(a) revokes EO 12891 by number and subject, and section 7 gives the express effective date 1997-09-30. Section 4(b) provides that the Committee terminates 30 days after submitting its final report to the Human Radiation Interagency Working Group. EO 12975 (signed 1995-10-03; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12975.txt, sha256 ac77dacc351be0b4d2f8076b11ee173b1c72207e77fd0c131e9b23987207b6e3) directs agencies to take account of "the recommendations con-" tained in the report of the Advisory Committee on Human Radiation Experiments, so a report of the Committee existed by 1995-10-03; EO 12975 does not say that this was the final report or when it was submitted to the Working Group, so the date on which the Committee terminated under section 4(b) is not fixed by a held source. If that report was the final report submitted on or before 1995-10-03, the Committee terminated no later than 1995-11-02 and the order was functionally spent by then. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, which reaches report-relative sunsets, this is a spent fact and not the end; it is not recorded as a dated later event because no exact date is held. Bounded search: the dossier's three machine searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts); the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md (it finds EO 13062 in its FR text, its APP mirror and a source-ladder copy as the only other texts citing the order); the U.S. Code hits are editorial notes under 42 U.S.C. 2210, stating that the order was revoked by EO 13062 section 3(a), and under 42 U.S.C. 6601, a memorandum referring to the order as formerly set out; the current-law mention table lists no eCFR mention, and neither search yields a current-law predicate; the catalog note reads "Revoked by: EO 13062, September 29, 1997"; and a literal search of held texts for Human Radiation, which found EO 12975.
